local.h: Georgia's Latino voters swing toward Democrats
local.b: About 198,000 Latinos voted in Georgia's midterms, up 78% from 2022, and polling showed 72% backed Sen. Jon Ossoff. Advocates warn it's a misalignment, not a realignment, and both parties must earn their votes.
local.title: Georgia’s Latinos shift toward Democratic candidates, for now

local.h: UN honors CNN founder Ted Turner
local.b: The United Nations held a celebration of life for Ted Turner, who died in May at 87. His daughter Laura Turner Seydel recalled his record $1 billion gift to UN causes in 1997 and urged guests to back the institutions that hold the world together.
local.title: UN honors late media mogul and CNN founder Ted Turner

local.h: Patrice Bergeron inducted into Hockey Hall of Fame
local.b: The longtime Bruins center joined Carey Price, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the Hall of Fame's 2026 class in Toronto.

local.h: Up to 300,000 in Mass. could lose insurance despite blue wave
local.b: Democrats' win in Congress won't quickly reverse federal Medicaid and ACA subsidy cuts that take effect as the new Congress arrives in January. State officials expect up to 300,000 Massachusetts residents to become uninsured.
local.title: What a blue Congress means — and doesn’t mean — for healthcare in Mass.

local.h: Ex-officer Farwell guilty of killing Sandra Birchmore
local.b: A federal jury convicted former Stoughton police officer Matthew Farwell of strangling 23-year-old Sandra Birchmore and her unborn child in her Canton apartment in 2021. Prosecutors said he killed her to hide that he had abused her since she was 15.

local.h: Lawmakers probe deadly fires at Joliet prison
local.b: State legislators held a hearing after a Marshall Project, WBEZ and Sun-Times investigation found 70 fires at the Joliet Treatment Center, where men in mental health care set fires in despair over conditions. Two died.
local.title: Lawmakers hold hearing on investigation into deadly Illinois prison fires

local.h: Police sergeant dies after being found unresponsive at station
local.b: Sgt. Timothy Martin, 49, was found unresponsive on duty at the Albany Park District station and later pronounced dead. The medical examiner hasn't ruled on a cause.
local.title: Chicago police sergeant dies after being found unresponsive at Northwest Side station

local.h: Amazon drone delivery center coming to Markham
local.b: Amazon says drone deliveries will start this fall from a new center at 2201 W. 159th St. in Markham, part of a suburban expansion. The drones carry packages up to five pounds.
local.title: Amazon drone delivery center in Markham set for takeoff

local.h: Morton Grove man died after deportation, lawyer says
local.b: Ayaz Ahmed, 61, who had chronic health conditions and needed a breathing device, died shortly after a deportation flight to Pakistan, his attorney said. He had been detained by ICE in June over an expired visa.

goodnews.h: Illinois Holocaust Museum reopens after renovation
goodnews.b: The Skokie museum reopens Wednesday after 15 months and more than $10 million in upgrades, including a reflection gallery, new artifacts and a 240-seat auditorium.
goodnews.title: ‘A sanctuary of memory’: Illinois Holocaust Museum and Education Center reopens in Skokie after 15-month renovation

local.h: Citywide upzoning back on the table in Denver
local.b: Denver's "Unlocking Housing Choices" proposal has been expanded once more, reviving a citywide upzoning push.
local.title: A citywide upzoning is back on the menu in Denver

local.h: Denver could close Crossroads shelter within a year
local.b: The city may sign a short contract with Urban Alchemy to run the Crossroads shelter while it looks for replacements.
local.title: Denver could close the Crossroads shelter in the next year

local.h: Denver passes $1.68 billion budget
local.b: The City Council passed Denver's 2027 budget, which grows slightly after years of cuts, though some members say it falls short in some areas.
local.title: Denver’s $1.68B budget passed. Council members weren’t thrilled about it

local.h: Shimell unseats Amezcua as Santa Ana mayor
local.b: Attorney Dan Shimell defeated incumbent Valerie Amezcua in one of Orange County's biggest upsets, holding a 5-point lead Tuesday night. Amezcua conceded on social media.
local.title: Dan Shimell unseats incumbent Valerie Amezcua as Santa Ana’s next mayor

local.h: Ballot tampering claim in tight South LA council race
local.b: Council District 9 candidate Estuardo Mazariegos filed a complaint alleging front-runner Jose Ugarte's campaign mishandled voters' ballots. The race remains too close to call.
local.title: In tight South LA race, one city council candidate accuses the other of alleged voter fraud

local.h: Claims center opens for Garden Grove evacuees
local.b: GKN Aerospace opened a center in Los Alamitos Tuesday to help residents evacuated during the Garden Grove chemical tank scare file for reimbursement from its $100 million claims program. Help is offered in English, Vietnamese, Spanish and Korean.

local.h: Teen arrested in killing of Bronx boy walking to school
local.b: Police arrested a 17-year-old in the Oct. 29 shooting death of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong near Crotona Park. The motive is not yet clear.
local.title: Teen arrested for fatal shooting of 15-year-old Bronx boy walking to school, NYPD says

local.h: Sanitation supervisors rack up speed camera tickets
local.b: Gothamist found 763 sanitation department cars assigned to supervisors and other staff have collected at least 2,375 speed camera tickets since 2023. Advocates want faster rollout of speed limiters, which Mayor Mamdani supports.
local.title: NYC sanitation supervisors keep speeding on the job, data shows

local.h: Chelsea NYCHA redevelopment splits Mamdani's allies
local.b: Tenant activists at Fulton and Elliott-Chelsea Houses have joined DSA to fight the $1.2 billion plan to replace about 2,000 public housing units with mixed-income development, calling it privatization. Mamdani says a teardown is cheaper than repairs.
local.title: Mamdani’s redevelopment plan for NYCHA complex in Chelsea spills into DSA

local.h: Ninth death in city jail custody this year
local.b: A man held at Rikers' Robert N. Davoren Center was found dead in his bed, at least the ninth death in Department of Correction custody this year. The department did not release a cause and will investigate.
local.title: Rikers detainee's death is at least the 9th in corrections department custody this year

local.h: Hochul keeps door open to redrawing House map
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul said Democratic gains don't necessarily end the push to amend the state constitution for mid-decade redistricting, which could let Democrats redraw New York's districts as soon as 2028, but she didn't commit.
local.title: Gov. Hochul keeps the door open to redrawing New York’s congressional map

local.h: Man indicted in killing of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez
local.b: Brooklyn prosecutors indicted a city Department of Education worker in the Oct. 30 stabbing of Katie Suarez on a Bath Beach path. Police say surveillance shows him fleeing the scene.
local.title: Man indicted in stabbing murder of Brooklyn runner Katie Suarez

local.h: Judge orders city to answer ICE shelter subpoena
local.b: A federal judge ruled City Hall must give ICE the names and birthdates of South Bronx migrant shelter residents with serious criminal histories. The Mamdani administration says it is evaluating next steps.
local.title: ICE subpoena puts a spotlight on the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC

local.h: Canal Street face-lift pushed into 2027
local.b: The city's Department of Transportation told a community board that concrete work on west Canal Street, planned for this fall, will slip to next year in the Reimagining Canal Street project.
local.title: Manhattan's Canal Street is getting a face-lift, but it'll take a while

local.h: East Harlem buildings head to auction despite City Hall push
local.b: Thirty-eight deteriorating buildings with about 850 mostly rent-stabilized apartments, formerly owned by bankrupt Emerald Equities Group, go to auction starting Tuesday. Mayor Mamdani's administration had backed a bid by affordable housing developer Spatial Equity to buy the portfolio first.
local.title: Rent-stabilized buildings hit auction block, despite Mamdani’s efforts to intervene

goodnews.h: Lost Georgia O'Keeffe painting found in East Village closet
goodnews.b: A niece helping her aunt settle her affairs found O'Keeffe's landscape "Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I" in a wooden box behind coats. Christie's specialists called the find exceptional.
goodnews.title: Long-lost Georgia O’Keeffe painting found in East Village closet

local.h: Russia bans two French lawmakers and two journalists
local.b: Moscow barred four French citizens in retaliation for France's July expulsion of former RT France head Xenia Fedorova, whom Paris called an agent of influence.
local.title: Russia bans two French lawmakers, two journalists in tit-for-tat move

local.h: Zemmour enters French presidential race
local.b: Far-right Reconquete leader Eric Zemmour declared his candidacy, pledging two million fewer immigrants by the end of a five-year term. Marine Le Pen remains widely projected to lead the first round.
local.title: French far-right politician Zemmour joins presidential race

local.h: BHV Marais abruptly shuts its doors
local.b: The Paris department store closed Monday evening after an insurance policy lapsed during its bankruptcy process. Management says a new contract takes effect Tuesday, but unions fear it won't reopen.

local.h: Ritz searched in Al-Fayed trafficking probe
local.b: Investigators searched the Ritz and other Paris landmarks tied to the late Mohamed Al-Fayed in a probe into accomplices in alleged human trafficking. People were held for questioning and his former Saint-Tropez estate was also investigated.

local.h: France summons Iran's envoy over fridge sabotage
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot summoned Iran's ambassador to protest the cyberattack on supermarket fridges, calling it the first large-scale sabotage attack on French territory. He said France will push for EU sanctions and rules nothing out.

local.h: France vows tough response to Iran-blamed supermarket cyberattack
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador will be summoned and EU sanctions sought over the October attack on hundreds of supermarket fridges.

local.h: Wilson approves targeted expansion of police cameras
local.b: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson will allow surveillance cameras in three more neighborhoods after pausing the plan last spring, saying an NYU Policing Project audit supports a targeted approach. Stadium District cameras activate immediately.

local.h: Federal prosecutors can't keep up with detention challenges
local.b: Facing a flood of habeas petitions from people saying they're unlawfully held by immigration authorities, the US Attorney's Office for Western Washington says it can no longer defend every case and will let judges rule without opposition.

local.h: Murray questions ICE's $1.5 billion Tacoma detention deal
local.b: Sen. Patty Murray, set to chair Senate Appropriations, is pressing DHS about ICE's $1.5 billion contract to keep a private firm running the Northwest ICE Processing Center and whether ICE still plans to buy a new Seattle-area facility.

goodnews.b: Gov. Bob Ferguson's office chose the Seattle guitar legend for the state's innovation coin, due in 2029.
